title: Lower semicontinuity of geometric component counts for proper flat spaces
statement: Let $T$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and $f:X\to T$ a proper flat morphism of finite presentation from an algebraic space [def-trf-algebraic-space, def-sfb-space-morphism-properties]. Finite presentation means local finite presentation on etale scheme charts, quasi-compactness, and quasi-separatedness. Use sheaf fibre products [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers] and the atlas point topology [def-a1-space-point-topology]. For each $t\in T$ choose an algebraic closure $\overline{\kappa(t)}$ of the residue field [def-weil-residue-field, def-weil-algebraic-closure], and let $n_f(t)$ be the number of maximal nonempty connected subsets of $X\times_T\operatorname{Spec}\overline{\kappa(t)}$. This number is finite. For every $t\in T$ there is an open neighbourhood $V$ of $t$ such that $n_f(u)\geq n_f(t)$ for every $u\in V$. Empty fibres have count zero. No reducedness hypothesis on the geometric fibres or Noetherian hypothesis on $T$ is imposed.

proof.text: For any $t\in T$, properness survives base change to $\operatorname{Spec}\overline{\kappa(t)}$. Apply the proper-space global-algebra theorem only in its unrestricted first clause: the component set is finite and its components are clopen. This does not require reducedness. It proves finiteness of $n_f(t)$, including zero for an empty fibre.

We will use invariance of the count under scheme base change. If $g:T'\to T$ and $t'\mapsto t$, choose algebraic closures $\Omega$ of $\kappa(t)$ and $\Omega'$ of $\kappa(t')$. Regard both as extensions of $\kappa(t)$ and embed them in a common field, then in its algebraic closure $M$. Reassociation of fibre products identifies the two resulting fibres over $M$. The separably closed component theorem applied to each algebraically closed field $\Omega,\Omega'$ gives component bijections with this common fibre. Thus $n_{f_{T'}}(t')=n_f(t)$. The same argument works for an arbitrary algebraically closed extension of the residue field.

Fix $t$. Restrict to an affine open neighbourhood $T_0=\operatorname{Spec}A$ of $t$, replacing $X$ by its pullback. Properness, flatness and finite presentation persist by the base-change locality theorem, and step 2 identifies the counts on $T_0$ with the original counts. Take the canonical factorization $X\xrightarrow q Z=\operatorname{Spec}\Gamma(X,\mathcal O_X)\xrightarrow\pi T_0$. The space Stein theorem gives integral $\pi$ and proper $q$ with nonempty geometrically connected fibres. The Stein-fibre theorem gives a finite set $\pi^{-1}(t)$ with finite residue extensions. Therefore integral-fibre etale splitting applies to $\pi$ at $t$: obtain an affine etale $g:U\to T_0$, $u\mapsto t$, and a finite clopen partition $Z_U=\coprod_{i=1}^m V_i$, where each $V_i$ has exactly one point $v_i$ over $u$ and $\kappa(v_i)/\kappa(u)$ is purely inseparable. Do not identify $m$ with the number of points of $Z$ over $t$ before this etale extension.

Let $X_U=X\times_{T_0}U$, and let $q_U:X_U\to Z_U$ be the pullback of $q$. Put $X_i=q_U^{-1}(V_i)$ as an open subspace: on a scheme test it is the inverse image of the open subscheme $V_i$. The open-subspace definition makes this an algebraic space. Continuity and the open-subspace topology show that these are a finite disjoint clopen partition of $X_U$. They remain such a partition after every scheme base change, since inverse images preserve unions, intersections and complements on scheme tests.

Set $k=\kappa(u)$ and choose its algebraic closure $\Omega$. The scheme $(V_i)_u$ has exactly one point and purely inseparable residue extension, hence is radicial. Universal injectivity gives at most one point in $(V_i)_\Omega$. There is at least one: in characteristic $p>0$, embed $\kappa(v_i)$ in $\Omega$ by sending $a$, with $a^{p^r}=c\in k$, to the unique root of $Z^{p^r}-c$. Increasing exponents proves independence, and a common exponent for two elements proves additivity and multiplicativity. In characteristic zero the extension is trivial. The resulting residue-field morphism supplies an $\Omega$-point. Write $z_i$ for the unique point. The fibre of $q_U$ after extension to $\Omega$ over $z_i$ is, by reassociating fibre products, a field-extension fibre of $q$. It is nonempty and connected by the Stein theorem. Apply the scheme-target fibre-topology theorem to identify it homeomorphically with the inverse image of $z_i$, which is all of $(X_i)_\Omega$. Thus every $(X_i)_\Omega$ is nonempty connected.

The geometric fibre over $u$ is partitioned by the $m$ nonempty connected clopen subsets $(X_i)_\Omega$. A connected subset meeting a clopen piece lies in that piece, because otherwise that piece and its complement separate the subset. Hence these pieces are exactly the maximal nonempty connected subsets. Step 2 yields $n_f(t)=m$. If $m=0$, the fibre is empty and the desired inequality holds on all of $T$ since counts are nonnegative; henceforth assume $m>0$.

The map $X_U\to U$ is flat and finitely presented by base-change locality. Each $X_i\to U$ is flat and locally of finite presentation. To check the restriction, use a surjective etale scheme chart $H\to X_U$ and its open inverse image $H_i$ of $X_i$. The chart test makes $H\to U$ flat and locally of finite presentation. The same local-ring maps prove flatness on $H_i$. At a point of $H_i$, choose a finite-presentation affine witness $\operatorname{Spec}C$ for $H\to U$ and shrink to a principal open $D(h)$ lying in $H_i$. If $C=R[x_1,\ldots,x_a]/(r_1,\ldots,r_b)$ then $C_h=R[x_1,\ldots,x_a,z]/(r_1,\ldots,r_b,zh-1)$ is finitely presented over $R$. The chart test back on $H_i\to X_i$ gives the claim. The universally-open theorem now says that $W_i=\operatorname{im}(|X_i|\to U)$ is open. It contains $u$ by step 5.

Put $W=\bigcap_{i=1}^mW_i$, an open neighbourhood of $u$. For $w\in W$, the point-image formula applied to $X_i\to U$ and $\operatorname{Spec}\overline{\kappa(w)}\to U$ shows that $(X_i)_{\bar w}$ is nonempty, since $w$ belongs to the image of $X_i$. Thus $(X_U)_{\bar w}$ is partitioned into $m$ nonempty clopen pieces. Each component lies in one piece, and each nonempty piece contains a component (the component of any one of its points), so $n_{f_U}(w)\ge m$. The scheme etale-open theorem makes $g$ open; therefore $V=g(W)$ is an open neighbourhood of $t$ in $T_0$, hence in $T$. For $v\in V$, choose $w\in W$ over $v$. Step 2 gives $n_f(v)=n_{f_U}(w)\ge m=n_f(t)$, as required.
